newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Gaddum - markets sometimes trigger concern.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Gaddum - markets sometimes trigger concern.

text.p: Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum said on Thursday that financial markets had taken on too powerful a role in recent years, which sometimes gave room for concern.

"Financial markets often appear to give cause for concern...For the financial markets increasingly seem to be divesting themselves of the 'subservient role' they are supposed to play," Gaddum said in a speech.
The speech, prepared for delivery to the 32nd Conference of the Governors of South-East Asian Central Banks in Bangkok, was made available here.
One problem Gaddum saw was that "anonymous market forces constrict policy makers' national room for manoeuvre."
On the other hand, this also has benefits as "the financial markets thereby lessen the scope for a monetary policy that is detrimental to stability and a fiscal policy that inflates debt".
At the same time, more sophisticated financial instruments coupled with advanced professionalism among fund managers could all be seen to raise the spectre of potential dangers.
But Gaddum also said "the greater international diversification of investments makes the markets fundamentally more resilient today."
Against the backdrop of such an environment, Gaddum warned that the world's central banks must focus on continuity to build confidence.
"Monetary policy itself must not be an uncertainty factor that fosters volatility. ... Continuity, consistency, credibility -- the three Cs denote the right direction."
